questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the University had courses that I found interesting. As Erasmus University of Rotterdam is placed in Rotterdam who has the biggest harbor in Europe, the University had a wide range of courses within sea and transportation law which my home university does not teach in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Throughout my exchange it has been very easy to navigate in the courses as the university representatives were very fast to respond to e-mails and other questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information about the possible courses as well as information about examination, including registration for the exam. Furthermore, we were provided with e-mails about a WhatsApp group for all international students that we could sign up for.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Be aware of the deadlines when it comes to registering for courses as well as examinations. It is possible to change a course during the semester

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a little bit difficult to find housing on my own but I found a private student housing company called HouseHunting. They were super professional and made it very easy for me. Another option is looking at Facebook groups. This is where I initially found out about the company I renting my room through. There are a lot of scammer so be aware of that when looking on social media.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus was a really great way to experience Rotterdam and was way more authentic than living on campus. With that being said, it also has a negative side as it makes it a bit more difficult to socialize with fellow students from Erasmus University. I was happy that I got to stay off campus but I can definitely see the advantages by living on campus - but be quick because there are not many rooms for exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy to register for exams as well as for the courses. You are able to change the courses you chose in the beginning.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The representative of the international students was really fast to respond and helped change my courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check all the courses including the examination format and date. I would recommend to have 2 courses per block. I had three courses one block which was a bit too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The programme was great but some courses are only offered in specific blocks so in that way it is a little bit limited.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is very high which I really enjoyed. Everybody participates in class and the professors often gives examples from own experience which is really interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same style where the professors went through the material and the students got to ask questions. We went through cases together. Each course is different as I also had some courses that were more interactive.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Trade Finance and Banking Law, Carriage of Goods, Charter Parties and Bills of Lading, EU Competition Law and Rule of Law in a Global Context.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can definitely recommend Trade Finance and Banking Law which is taught by Johan Vannerom and Frank Stevens. Both professors are very skilled. Frank Stevens also has the class Charter Parties and Bills of Lading which was a great course as well. This course as well as Carriage of Goods are about sea and transportation law which I actually enjoyed learning about. The first three courses works very well together.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries is a little bit more expensive than in Denmark but having a beer on a bar is half the price.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student organisation ESN arranges a lot of events every week, e.g. parties and sportsevents.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend participating in some of the weekly activities from ESN as well as the introduction week that is also arranged by ESN.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You have to experience the nearest cities. Don't just go to Amsterdam - its a great city but so is Rotterdam, Den Haag and the other nearby cities. I also visited Bruxelles which is only 1,5 hour away by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very similar to the danish culture so it was very easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't just stay at Campus. Join a local football club or your local gym.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really the biggest differences besides the nightlife. In the Netherlands it is more including.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Dutch people are the sweetest! They are super helpful and everybody speaks perfect english - even the older ones.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress it, have fun and enjoy it while it last!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to get out of your comfort zone from the beginning. People start socializing early on and you don't want to miss out on that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic level was very high and I learned something that I would not have been able to at UCPH.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Socializing when living outside of campus but it is not impossible - just takes a little bit more effort.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: As a master student at my 10th semester, I found that people were quite young. The average age was around 21. In hindsight I would probably have enjoyed it more if I was at my bachelor.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
